questions.prompt: For S = 100, K = 100, T = 1, r = 5% and σ = 20%, d1 is 0.35. What is d2?
The volatility input rises from 20% to 30%, and the call rises from $10.45 to $14.23. Why does more volatility raise the price?
options: Because a wider spread of outcomes gives more chances of a large payoff, while the loss stays capped at the premium
Because volatility raises the stock price
Because the risk-free rate rises with volatility
Because the strike falls when volatility rises
questions.explanation: The option pays more in large up moves but never less than zero in down moves. So a wider spread of outcomes adds value.

questions.prompt: Which of the five inputs cannot be observed directly in the market?
options: The future volatility of the stock
questions.explanation: The stock price, strike, time and rate are all known today. The volatility of the stock until expiry is in the future, so it must be estimated.
